adjudication: Three independent readers agreed EXACTLY on the accent layer: 6 anudatta + 4 svarita = 10, with identical (word_index, aksara_index, type) tuples for all 10 marks (verified programmatically). All three also independently found the same hard case: the sixth anudatta bar is set ~14-16 px BELOW the other five (y2076-2086 vs y2059-2073) because the printer had to clear the vocalic-R hook of the N+NR conjunct. S1 corroborated the habit on line 3 of the same leaf, where bars under TR and VR are dropped the same way. Two aksara identities were disputed, both ADJUDICATED FROM THE SCAN by side-by-side composite against controls taken from the same printed line: (1) word 4: AYAM (S1) vs AGRAM (S2, S3). Adopted AGRAM. The disputed glyph was composited against the certain YA of word 3 on the same line: the certain YA is a compact left bowl with a thin crescent counter joining the stem horizontally at the foot, whereas the disputed glyph has an open upper-left hook plus a prominent bold diagonal descending below the body line - a subscript RA. Majority and image agree. (2) word 3: ANAYADVACO (S1, S2) vs ANAYANVACO (S3). Adopted ANAYANVACO, OVERRIDING the 2-1 majority. The conjunct at x966-1070 was composited against plain NA (x1550-1628), plain DA (x2195-2262) and plain VA (x2128-2196) from the same line. The conjunct's upper member is a left blob with a horizontal bar running right and white above it - identical to plain NA - while plain DA on this line is a hook curving down-left with a rounded terminal and NO rightward bar. The lower member matches plain VA. S1 had justified DVA by claiming the upper member repeats the left wedge plus rightward bar of the plain DA, but the DA on this line has no rightward bar at all; that feature is diagnostic of NA. Both S1 and S2 had already flagged this conjunct as their least certain glyph. Neither disputed locus affects any mark tuple.
boundary_interpretation: WORD SEGMENTATION. I took the sirorekha runs at y 1958 and y 1962 as primary evidence and cross-checked against body-column runs over y 1975-2030. The sirorekha breaks fall into two clearly separated populations: intra-word letter joins of 4-12 px, and inter-word gaps of 38-49 px. Applying a 38px floor the line segments into nine words plus punctuation: [0] dhiitii x 187-409, [1] vaa x 449-567, [2] ye x 607-679, [3] anayadvaacho x 720-1210, [4] agram x 1249-1431, [5] manasaa x 1470-1744, [6] vaa x 1784-1903, [7] ye x 1941-2015, [8] avagraha+vadannrtaani x 2065-2562; then danda x 2606-2622, double-danda x 2875-2913, numeral 1 x 2961-3009, double-danda x 3059-3096. The avagraha (x 2065-2110) is separated from the preceding ye by 49px but from the following va by only 10px, so I attached it to the following word as printed, giving word [8]. word_index runs over those nine Devanagari words only; the danda, double-dandas and verse numeral are punctuation and get no word index (no mark falls near them). AKSARA INDEXING. I enumerate printed glyph cells left to right. Inside word [8] the avagraha is counted as aksara_index 0, so va=1, da=2, na-nr=3, taa=4, ni=5. If a comparison convention excludes the avagraha from the aksara count, subtract 1 from every aksara_index in word [8]. MARKS NEAR A BOUNDARY. This print sets the anudatta bar under the left-of-centre part of its aksara, and the svarita tick directly over that aksara's right-hand vertical stem; every assignment below is a containment test against measured glyph columns. x 226 (bar 207-245): dhii occupies x 195-290, tii x 306-396 - wholly inside dhii, not near a boundary. x 494 (bar 476-512): the single-aksara word vaa occupies x 461-556; unambiguous. x 871 (tick 866-877): na occupies x 820-892 with its own stem at x 872-880, and the sirorekha breaks at x 893-896 before ya. The tick stands over na's stem, 22px clear of the break, so it is na's and not ya's. x 1014 (bar 995-1033): ya occupies x 897-963, the dva conjunct x 968-1070 (its aa stem 1053-1070). The bar lies entirely right of ya's right edge and its centre is within 12px of dva's centre. This is the closest of the six bars; assigned to dva. x 1400 (bar 1379-1420): a occupies x 1250-1350, gram x 1353-1428. The bar is wholly right of 1353, and the anusvara dot of gram (x 1397-1422) stands directly above it at the same x, so dot and bar belong to the same aksara. Assigned to gram. x 1607 (tick 1601-1613): inside manasaa (ma 1477-1550, na 1554-1620, sa 1626-1697, aa 1713-1731) the tick falls inside na. x 1828 (bar 1810-1848): the single-aksara word vaa occupies x 1796-1890; unambiguous. x 2177 (tick 2171-2184): va occupies x 2132-2198 with its stem at x 2178-2188 and da begins at x 2199. The tick is over va's stem, so va's and not da's. x 2311 (bar 2290-2330): the na-nr aksara occupies roughly x 2270-2330 and owns the vocalic-r hook at x 2300-2344; da is x 2199-2266 and its tail ends at x 2266 / y 2056. The bar lies entirely right of 2266 and directly under the na-nr cell, so it is na-nr's and not da's. x 2542 (tick 2536-2549): ni occupies x 2461-2556 - the short-i matra arc is x 2463-2522 and na's right stem is x 2537-2555. The tick stands over that stem and is 50px clear of the danda at x 2606, so it is ni's, and it is the last mark on the line.
dissent: Read word 3 as ANAYADVACO. OVERRULED from the scan; S2 had itself listed this conjunct as unclear, read as DVA by elimination.
notes: MAGNIFICATION AND METHOD. I read the two supplied 1568px segment crops, re-rendered the same line at 4 segments with scripts/crop_atharvaveda_line.py, then cut my own PIL crops of the same line at x3 to x10 (LANCZOS) around every candidate. All positions and sizes reported here were measured on the source raster itself (leaf 4000x5959; find_text_block box 482,362-3618,5448; block 3136x5086) via row-ink projection, per-row/per-column ink maps, and 8-connected component extents at thresholds 128, 150 and 175. ACCEPTED MARKS. Six anudatta: flat dashes 36-40px wide by 9-11px tall (aspect about 3.7:1) at x 207-245, 476-512, 995-1033, 1379-1420, 1808-1849 in the band y 2058-2073, plus one at x 2290-2330 / y 2077-2087. Four svarita: upright strokes 10-13px wide by 29-37px tall (aspect about 1:3) at x 866-877, 1601-1613, 2171-2184, 2536-2549, all rising from the top of my sirorekha into the band y 1914-1951. All ten are stable across thresholds 128-175. REJECTED FALSE POSITIVES, BY SHAPE. (1) x 2300-2344, y 2036-2074, 45x39 - a curved hook, the vocalic-r descender of the na-nr aksara: rejected as anudatta because it is curved and 39px tall, i.e. taller than wide, and runs continuously up into the glyph body with no white gap. It is why the sixth real bar sits 15px lower than the other five. At threshold 175 hook and bar merge into one component; at 128 and 150 they are separate, and the raw pixel map shows a clear light row at y 2075-2076 between them, so the bar is a genuinely separate mark. (2) x 2232-2265, y 2032-2056, 34x24 - the diagonal tail of the da in vadan-, continuous with its glyph body, no white gap, diagonal not flat. (3) Five wide curved matras above the headline, all rejected on width: x 228-285 (ii of dhii), 337-392 (ii of tii), 608-668 (e of ye), 1120-1191 (o of cho), 2462-2523 (short i of ni) - 55 to 72px across, against 10-13px for a svarita. The control is dhiitii, where the ii is printed as a broad arch above the headline whose right leg descends to the baseline; none of my four ticks carries any arch. (4) x 1397-1422, y 1924-1947, 26x24 - the anusvara of gram: a diamond dot about as wide as tall, not an upright stroke. (5) A faint horizontal smudge that appeared under ye / avagraha around x 2058-2096, y 2037-2047 in a LANCZOS render: the raw pixel map of x 2040-2115, y 2034-2059 is entirely blank (all values above 190). A resampling artefact on paper texture, not ink. (6) At threshold 175 three specks appear in the bar band - x 2157-2163 (7x6), x 2530-2538 (9x8), x 2556-2562 (7x4); all far below the 20-45px anudatta width and all gone at 150. Speckle. (7) Verso show-through is visible between the danda at x 2606-2622 and the double-danda at x 2875-2913; it is grey, unfocused and mirrored, and carries no mark. LINE ATTRIBUTION. The brief's central trap does not bite on this line: the line above is a short centred heading confined to x 941-2353 with no sirorekha, and the gutter between it and mine (y 1862-1913) carries zero ink at threshold 170, so nothing in my supra-headline band can be a bar from the line above. Symmetrically, the next line's supra band does not start until y 2091 with rows y 2088-2090 empty, so my displaced bar at y 2077-2087 cannot belong to it - and it is flat, whereas anything of the next line's in that band would be one of its own upright strokes or a wide matra. UNCLEAR (2), both glyph-identity doubts rather than accent doubts. (a) The stacked conjunct at x 968-1050 read as dva: the lower member is plainly va (closed loop plus stem), the upper member is a reduced half-form I read as da by elimination and it could conceivably be another dental. (b) The stacked conjunct at x 2270-2330 read as n-na: two na-like members on one stem with the vocalic r below; at the 2024px native resolution the upper member's identity is at the limit of the raster. Neither doubt changes the mark count or the carrier assignment, since in both cases the mark sits under the single stacked cell. The standalone vowel at x 722-817 and x 1250-1350 is read as a per the brief's fount note, though to a modern eye it reads as vocalic r or shra. I consulted no external text, edition, database or web resource, and I did not read or run the detector or binder scripts, nor anything under data/transcriptions/atharvaveda_bsb_1856/, nor any sibling reader directory. Where memory of the Atharvaveda suggested a reading I checked it against the ink; what is reported is what the ink shows. Spacing note: text_devanagari uses single spaces throughout, but as printed the gap between the single danda (x 2606-2622) and the double danda (x 2875-2913) is about 253px, some six times a normal word space.
